observations.text: SP, on first exposure to the high-G portion of the profile, performed the AGSM only after the IP directed its initiation and did not verify anti G suit operation before the first loaded turn. G loading was monitored by the IP throughout, and altitude excursions reaching 350 feet during the loaded turns were corrected on the IP's direction. Performance is at the desired standard for the Training Section but marginal, in that every G entry required IP direction. Independent recognition of the G onset and a self-initiated AGSM are expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP, with the IP's verbal prompts only and without the IP directing or executing any part of the sequence, initiated the AGSM before each G onset and confirmed anti G suit operation prior to the working phase. G loading was held at the briefed values, with altitude deviations reaching 300 feet and airspeed deviations reaching 20 knots at the recoveries, recognized and corrected with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP initiated the AGSM ahead of each G onset without IP prompting and maintained awareness of G loading during all maneuvers, keeping the applied G at the briefed values. Minor errors in straining cycle timing on the second and third entries produced altitude deviations of 220 feet and an exit heading deviation of 8 degrees, all recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP verified anti G suit operation before the working phase and performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, establishing the straining cycle before each G onset. Awareness of G loading was maintained during all maneuvers requiring more than 3 G, with the applied G at the briefed values and no approach to the A/C G-limits. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 7 knots and exit headings within 4 degrees, accurately and without hesitation. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP verified anti G suit operation, then performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual with the straining cycle fully established before every G onset. G loading was monitored continuously and matched the briefed values on each entry, well clear of the A/C G-limits. Deviations were negligible, with altitude held within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees across the whole high-G portion of the profile. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to initiating the anti-G straining maneuver only after the G onset instead of establishing it before the load, did not perform the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Awareness of G loading was not maintained through the turn reversal, with the result that the IP directed the unload and flew part of the recovery. The altitude excursion reached 450 feet before the aircraft was returned to the briefed altitude.

SP, due to an anti-G straining maneuver inadequate for the G applied, did not sustain the straining cycle through the loaded portion of the maneuver and reported grey-out symptoms on the second entry. Awareness of G loading was lost at that point, with the result that the IP took control and unloaded the aircraft. The recovery was completed by the IP with an altitude loss of 500 feet from the briefed altitude.

SP initiated the AGSM before each G onset and confirmed anti G suit operation, completing the high-G portion of the profile with the IP's verbal prompts and without IP intervention on the controls. Straining cycle timing was corrected twice after the IP called it, with deviations reaching 300 feet in altitude and 18 knots in airspeed, recognized and corrected with delay. Performance is at the desired standard for the Training Section but marginal, since the corrections followed the IP's calls rather than the SP's own assessment. Earlier self-recognition of G loading is expected on the following sorties.

SP performed the AGSM without IP prompting, verified anti G suit operation before the working phase and kept the applied G at the briefed values, clear of the A/C G-limits. Small errors in sustaining the straining cycle through the roll reversals led to altitude deviations of 200 feet and airspeed deviations of 14 knots, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP verified anti G suit operation and performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, with the straining cycle established before each G onset and sustained until the unload. Awareness of G loading was maintained during all maneuvers requiring more than 3 G, with the applied G matching the briefed values. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and exit headings within 5 degrees, accurately and without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP set up and verified anti G suit operation before the working phase and applied the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual on every entry, adjusting the straining effort to the G being applied. G loading was tracked continuously and remained at the briefed values with a wide margin to the A/C G-limits. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 4 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to omitting the anti-G suit connection and inflation check during the pre-maneuver checks, did not ensure proper anti G suit operation before the first loaded turn. The AGSM was then flown without suit assistance and awareness of G loading degraded through the maneuver, with the result that the IP directed the check and took control to reset the profile. Airspeed at the recovery was 35 knots below the briefed entry value and the altitude excursion reached 400 feet.

SP, due to reported inadequate rest and hydration before a high-G profile, did not sustain an effective AGSM at the G required by the maneuver and did not maintain awareness of G loading during the second half of the working phase. The result was that the IP directed the unload and flew the recovery, with the aircraft 380 feet below the briefed altitude at the wings-level point. The high-G portion of the profile was terminated by the IP.

SP, due to a straining cycle held for longer than the interval prescribed in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, did not maintain an effective AGSM through the sustained-G turns. Awareness of G loading was retained, but the correction of the straining technique and the return to the briefed parameters followed the IP's verbal prompts, with delay. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and the exit heading was 10 degrees off the briefed value, with no IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to attention captured by the pitch reference on the horizon while G loading went unmonitored, did not maintain awareness of G loading during the loaded portion of the maneuver and allowed the applied G to rise above the briefed value. Recognition came only after the IP's verbal prompts and the correction was made with delay, without IP intervention on the controls. Airspeed deviation at the exit reached 20 knots and the exit heading was 10 degrees off the briefed value.

SP verified anti G suit operation and performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, keeping the applied G at the briefed values and clear of the A/C G-limits. Minor errors in sustaining the straining cycle on the last two entries produced altitude deviations of 230 feet and an exit heading deviation of 8 degrees, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Performance is within the desired standard for the Training Section but marginal, as the same error repeated on consecutive entries. Consistency of the straining cycle through sustained G is expected to improve.

SP ensured proper anti G suit operation before the working phase and performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, establishing the straining cycle before each G onset. Awareness of G loading was maintained during all maneuvers requiring more than 3 G, with the applied G at the briefed values and no approach to the A/C G-limits. Altitude was held within 90 feet, airspeed within 6 knots and exit headings within 3 degrees, with accurate and prompt control inputs. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP checked anti G suit operation before the working phase and applied the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, matching the straining effort to the G onset rate on every entry. G loading was monitored continuously and the applied G was held at the briefed values throughout, with a comfortable margin to the A/C G-limits. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 45 feet, airspeed within 3 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees, and the profile was flown with no loss of capacity for the remaining cockpit tasks. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt aft stick input at the entry of the loaded turn, did not control the G onset rate and did not avoid exceeding A/C G-limits, the exceedance being confirmed on the G-meter. The AGSM had not been established before the load, with the result that the IP took control and unloaded the aircraft. The maneuver was terminated 450 feet below the briefed altitude and 30 knots below the briefed airspeed.

SP, due to overconfidence in the margin available at that airspeed and bank, did not maintain awareness of G loading during the maneuver and applied G beyond the briefed value without an AGSM matched to the load. The result was that the IP directed the unload and flew part of the recovery to keep the aircraft within A/C G-limits. At the wings-level point the aircraft was 400 feet below the briefed altitude and the exit heading was 25 degrees off.

SP, due to not cross-checking the G-meter during the loaded portion of the maneuver, did not maintain awareness of G loading and allowed the applied G to drift above the briefed value on two entries. The AGSM was performed, but was adjusted to the actual load only after the IP's verbal prompts and the correction was made with delay. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and airspeed deviation reached 20 knots at the exit, with no IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to continuation of the maneuver after the first symptom of reduced G-tolerance had been felt, did not unload as prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not maintain awareness of G loading through the recovery. The unload was initiated only on the IP's verbal directive and was applied with delay, without IP intervention on the controls. The exit heading was 10 degrees off the briefed value and altitude deviation reached 300 feet.

SP, due to relaxing the straining cycle at the start of the recovery while G was still applied, did not perform the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual through the full loaded portion of the maneuver. Anti-G suit operation was verified and the applied G stayed at the briefed values, clear of the A/C G-limits. The error produced an altitude deviation of 210 feet and an airspeed deviation of 15 knots at the exit, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not maintain continuous awareness of G loading and allowed the straining cycle to lapse briefly at the highest G of the maneuver. The lapse was self-detected and the AGSM was re-established without IP intervention. Deviations were limited to 180 feet in altitude and 7 degrees in exit heading, corrected in a timely manner.

SP ensured proper anti G suit operation and performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, maintaining awareness of G loading during all maneuvers and staying clear of the A/C G-limits. Altitude was held within 140 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and exit headings within 5 degrees, at the outer edge of the desired standard. Performance meets the standard required for the Training Section but is marginal, with the straining cycle re-established late on two of the six loaded entries. Tighter control of the G onset at the entry and a more consistent straining cycle are expected on the next sorties.

SP ensured proper anti G suit operation and performed the AGSM in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual on every entry, matching the straining effort to the G onset rate without prompting. Awareness of G loading was maintained throughout the profile, with the applied G held at the briefed values and a clear margin to the A/C G-limits, and the G-meter was cross-checked after each maneuver. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 4 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.
